# Yields keep rising, Novo's tough week, why cat product sales are surging and more in Morning Squawk

Published Fri, Sep 25 2026 8:39 AM EDT

[Alex Harring](https://www.cnbc.com/alex-harring/) [@alex\_harring](https://twitter.com/@alex_harring)

[WATCH LIVE](https://www.cnbc.com/live-tv?trknav=watchliveamparticleheader)

_This is CNBC's Morning Squawk newsletter._ [_Subscribe here_](https://www.cnbc.com/newsletter/morning-squawk/) _to receive future editions in your inbox._

Happy Friday. Your morning cup of joe may soon get harder to find, as [Starbucks](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SBUX) [closes more of its stores](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/starbucks-to-close-250-stores.html).

[Stock futures](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) are slightly higher this morning following a [muted day](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/23/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) for the market.

Ad

Here are five key things investors need to know to start the trading day:

## 1\. Feeling 22

![NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 05: Stock market numbers are displayed on the New York Stock Exchange during morning trading on August 05, 2026 in New York City. ](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108345504-1785952760573-gettyimages-2289192477-mms15378_ienmvr1q.jpeg?v=1785953356&w=720&h=405)

NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 05: Stock market numbers are displayed on the New York Stock Exchange during morning trading on August 05, 2026 in New York City.

Michael M. Santiago \| Getty Images News \| Getty Images

Treasury yields took center stage on Wall Street this week as they rocketed to [highs not seen in decades](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/us-treasury-yields-bonds-fed-inflation.html). Now, traders are assessing what the moves mean for a swath of assets and wondering whether yields' rapid climb is an omen that something could break in the market.

Here's the latest:

- The [30-year Treasury](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US30Y) yield hit its [highest level since 2004](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/us-treasury-yields-bonds-fed-inflation.html) yesterday. The [10-year note](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US10Y) also continued to rise, building on its biggest single-day jump in over a year.
- History shows that a sharp upswing in yields should be [just as concerning for investors](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/history-shows-financial-calamities-occur-when-rates-rise-rapidly-like-this-something-always-breaks.html) as any multiyear highs. As one analyst told CNBC, "We should be prepared or forewarned that rates are rising and something is going to break."
- CNBC's [Matt Peterson](https://www.cnbc.com/matt-peterson/) writes that rising yields are [offering a reality check](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/treasury-yields-warsh-bessent-fed-national-debt-analysis.html) for the U.S., as it grapples with persistent inflation and a growing debt pile. They're also exposing the tension between Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
- The average rate on the 30-year fixed mortgage [jumped to 7.45%](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/30-year-fixed-mortgage-rate-spikes-thursday-to-7point45percent.html) yesterday, according to Mortgage News Daily. Experts warn that increasing yields will also lead to higher [car loan interest rates.](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/car-loan-rates-may-rise-as-treasury-yields-climb.html)
- Despite pressure from the Treasury market, the [S&P 500](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.SPX) is still on track to post its first winning week in three. The [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.DJI), meanwhile, is set to log its fourth straight week of losses.
- [Follow live market updates here.](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)

## 2\. Downdraft

![The Speaker's chair sits empty during the first session of the 119th Congress, ahead of the vote for Speaker of the House in the House Chamber at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, on January 3, 2025.](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108081966-1735924968457-gettyimages-2191692307-AFP_36RZ6M8.jpeg?v=1735925042&w=720&h=405)

The Speaker's chair sits empty during the first session of the 119th Congress, ahead of the vote for Speaker of the House in the House Chamber at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, on January 3, 2025.

Mandel Ngan \| Afp \| Getty Images

The Senate voted down a resolution that would have called for an end to the Iran war [by a razor-thin margin](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/iran-war-powers-senate-vote-fuel.html) yesterday. All but four Republican senators voted against the measure, even as the GOP grapples with concerns that the conflict — and its effect on energy prices — could hinder its candidates' chances in the midterm elections.

The largest U.S. business groups this week cautioned Trump [against a diesel export ban](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/chamber-commerce-business-roundtable-trump-diesel-export-ban-iran-war.html), which the president has said he's pushed for amid the run-up in energy costs. Industry members have warned that such a move could [ultimately raise diesel costs](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/23/trump-diesel-export-ban-gas-prices.html).

Meanwhile, [oil prices are lower](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/25/oil-falls-as-potential-diplomatic-solution-to-iran-conflict-arises.html) this morning after Iranian state media reported that Tehran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, said the country [would reopen the Strait of Hormuz](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/25/us-iran-trump-hormuz-.html) within seven days "if certain conditions are met."

## 3\. Novo vs. Lilly

The logo of pharmaceutical company Novo Nordisk is displayed in front of its offices in Bagsvaerd, Copenhagen, Denmark, Feb. 4, 2026.

Tom Little \| Reuters

[Novo](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVO) gave a look into its plan to fuel growth beyond its blockbuster weight loss drugs this week. But as CNBC's [Annika Kim Constantino](https://www.cnbc.com/annika-kim-constantino/) and [Elsa Ohlen](https://www.cnbc.com/elsa-ohlen/) write, the drugmaker still has work to do to convince investors [it can hold its own](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/25/novo-eli-lilly-obesity-drugs.html) as [Eli Lilly](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/LLY) chips away at the Danish drugmaker's market share.

The drugmaker enjoyed an early lead in the oral weight loss market, thanks to its Wegovy pill, but Lilly CEO Dave Ricks told CNBC earlier this week that one-third of new GLP-1 patients are taking its Foundayo pill. Novo on Monday assured investors that it would have a pipeline of drugs — including some outside of its core obesity and diabetes area — that could enter the market with a bang.

U.S.-listed shares of Novo have dropped more than 10% so far this week, putting the stock on track for its worst performance since February. At the same time, Lilly shares have climbed about 2.5%.

## 4\. Charming Wall Street

Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive officer of Meta Platforms Inc., reveals the Muse Charm device during the Meta Connect event in Menlo Park, California, US, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026.

Minh Connors \| Bloomberg \| Getty Images

[Meta](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/META) was late to the generative artificial intelligence race. Now, Wall Street is rewarding the company's efforts to make sure [history doesn't repeat itself](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/meta-mark-zuckerberg-muse-charm-openai-agent.html) in the consumer AI game.

After revealing its personal agent app Muse earlier this month, the Facebook parent this week unveiled its Muse Charm device in an apparent bid to get ahead of OpenAI and [Google](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/GOOGL). As CNBC's [Jonathan Vanian](https://www.cnbc.com/jonathan-vanian/) writes, the device also reflects Meta's efforts to reduce its reliance on [Apple](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AAPL) for distribution.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg offered few specifics on what the gadget would actually do, but that didn't seem to discourage investors. Meta shares have soared nearly 17% this week, on track for their biggest weekly rally since early 2024.

## 5\. Look what the cat dragged in

A cat and a dog beside a Chewy shipping box outside a house in Germantown, New York, on Feb. 20, 2024.

Angus Mordant \| Bloomberg \| Getty Images

Cat owners are [splashing out](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/cat-ownership-food-sales-dog-demand.html) for their feline friends. It's a treat for pet retailers like [Chewy](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/CHWY), [General Mills](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/GIS) and [Petco](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/WOOF).

The American Pet Products Association estimated that 53 million households owned a cat in 2025 following a recent surge. Executives attributed the rise to the animals' ability to live in smaller spaces and their lower care costs relative to those of dogs.

Strength in cat product sales can cushion softness in the dog space. As Chewy CEO Sumit Singh put it on an earnings call this month: "Dog seems to be worsening; cat seems to be strengthening."
